title: Pulstar
subtitle: A careful route through alien space
summary: Pulstar is Aicom's horizontally scrolling shooter, released for Neo Geo arcades in Japan on 28 August 1995.
body: Pulstar is Aicom's horizontally scrolling shooter, released for Neo Geo arcades in Japan on 28 August 1995. The Dino246 spacecraft crosses eight stages to confront an alien threat to the Solar System. Enemy formations, projectiles and moving obstacles demand a carefully judged route, with a boss at the end of each stage. Its charged weapons and protective equipment give the player several tools, but survival depends on understanding how the next obstacle fits into the limited space around the ship.

Holding the fire button builds a charge shown on a meter. One portion produces a powerful focused shot, while another enables a rapid barrage, allowing the player to prepare a response before an enemy arrives. An auxiliary drone blocks fire and can ram smaller opponents. Sacrificing it creates a powerful explosion, exchanging continuing protection for an immediate advantage. Power-ups add speed and supporting craft. The choices remain connected: using a defensive resource to clear a dangerous moment changes the equipment available for the passage that follows.

Pulstar was the first Neo Geo game to incorporate three-dimensional pre-rendered visuals, producing detailed ships and environments within a two-dimensional shooter. Harumi Fujita and Yasuaki Fujita composed the music. The game reached AES that September and Neo Geo CD in October. Its severe challenge made learning routes particularly important, while its visual technique gave those routes a distinctive density. Yumekobo's later Blazing Star developed the approach with a broader choice of ships and a more forgiving balance, making Pulstar the demanding starting point of that short lineage.
